Never drop any rung below 10% in steady state.** | `link-adaptation` §10.2 |\n273\t| D18b | **Phase 5: adapt ladder weights from LOCAL metrics only — OLLA structure, 1:9 up/down asymmetry, ~1 s window, 2 s dwell, immediate hard step-down** | Closed-loop density control oscillates; profile selection stays a **stateless lookup** so there is no state machine to get stuck in. \"Local\" means the sender's own signals (frame timing, accelerometer à la COBRA), never receiver feedback. | `link-adaptation` §10.3 |\n274\t| D18c | **Assume 20–30% residual erasure. This is an ASSUMPTION about the channel, not a controlled target.** | Nothing in v1 observes erasure (D18a), so calling it a \"target\" was wrong. 20–30% is the evidence base's figure; driving it lower would mean the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused. Dwell is sized to survive the **top** of the band (§8.1), and the repair code (§8.2) covers the tail beyond it. | `link-adaptation` §9.3 |\n275\t\n276\t---\n277\t\n278\t## 5. Invariants\n279\t\n280\tViolating one of these is a correctness bug, not a tuning choice. Each has an\n281\tenforcement mechanism, because an invariant nothing checks is a comment.\n282\t\n283\t| # | Invariant | Enforced by |\n284\t|---|---|---|\n285\t| **I1** | Fragment length **L** MUST NOT change within a session (D15) | Session type makes `L` `readonly`; property test asserts a mid-session change throws |\n286\t| **I2** | The degree distribution and the decoder MUST change together (D6); any distribution change MUST be simulated before merge | `sim/` assertions ported into the test suite; CI gate G4 |\n287\t| **I3** | Fountain indices MUST be derived from `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`, never transmitted (D7) | Golden test vector `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set`, bit-exact across implementations |\n288\t| **I4** | The file MUST NOT be fully materialised in memory on either side (D20) | Phase 1 flat-memory test over a synthetic 4 GB stream |\n289\t| **I5** | **Exactly one payload block is GE-active at a time; the manifest stream has its own separate GE context** (bf-28b) | Session type permits two concurrent GE contexts: `active` for payload blocks and `manifestActive` for manifest blocks. Payload block-switch policy (`bf-2t1k`) governs when to switch: hold until rank K or N consecutive higher-index packets (default N=32). The manifest uses reserved `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF` and `PacketFlags.Manifest`, providing clean separation from payload blocks. This is necessary because manifest blocks are interleaved with payload blocks (§7.6), and both require fountain decoding. |\n290\t| **I6a** | **Block-layer** working set MUST stay ≤ 1 MB regardless of file size (264 KB at the adopted design) | A5 headless block-layer memory assertion |\n291\t| **I6b** | **Whole-receiver** peak MUST stay ≤ 64 MB, and the decode pool MUST hold ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s | Phase 3 instrumented run. A single 1080p RGBA frame is **7.9 MiB**, so this budget is dominated by the camera path, not the codec — which is why I6 had to be split |\n292\t| **I7** | Frames MUST be generated on demand, never pre-rendered (D24) | Ring buffer is bounded at 3; assertion on buffer depth |\n293\t| **I8** | A packet failing `fcrc` or `streamId` MUST be discarded, never applied | Unit test with corrupted and foreign packets |\n294\t| **I9** | A block MAY be written to OPFS before its hash arrives, but MUST NOT be surfaced to the user until verified | Test: blocks written before manifest arrives are not exported; verification failure prevents completion and triggers E-BLOCK-HASH |\n295\t| **I10** | Decoded output MUST be byte-identical to input | End-to-end property test, every phase |\n296\t\n297\t---\n298\t\n299\t## 6. Architecture\n300\t\n301\t### 6.1 Layering\n302\t\n303\t**Modulation is swappable**, and **the block layer bounds everything below it**.\n304\t\n305\t```\n306\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n307\t│ UI          role select · progress · file in/out · coach │\n308\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n309\t│ Session     metadata · compression · resume · verify     │\n310\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n311\t│ Block       file ⇄ 192 KB blocks · scheduling · bitmap   │\n312\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n313\t│ Fountain    LT encode (endless) / GF(2) GE decode        │\n314\t│             K = 768 · matrix 72.0 KB · CONSTANT          │\n315\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n316\t│ Framing     13-byte header + payload → packet bytes      │\n317\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n318\t│ Modulation  ◄──────────────────────── SWAPPABLE ────────►│\n319\t│   Stage 1   tiled monochrome QR                          │\n320\t│   Stage 2   + RGB channel tripling                       │\n321\t│   Stage 3   libcimbar-derived grid codec                 │\n322\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n323\t│ Transport   canvas render loop  /  camera capture loop   │\n324\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n325\t```\n326\t\n327\t```ts\n328\tinterface Modulation {\n329\t  readonly packetsPerFrame: number;     // 1 plain, ~15 tiled, ~45 tripled\n330\t  readonly bytesPerPacket: number;      // = 13 + L\n331\t  encodeFrame(packets: Uint8Array[]): ImageData;\n332\t  decodeFrame(frame: VideoFrame): Uint8Array[];   // 0..n — never throws\n333\t}\n334\t```\n335\t\n336\t`decodeFrame` returning fewer packets than `packetsPerFrame` is the **normal case**.\n337\tNothing above this layer may care.\n338\t\n339\t### 6.2 Threads and ownership\n340\t\n341\tLayer boundaries and thread boundaries are **not** the same, which is worth stating\n342\texplicitly because it is a common source of bugs:\n343\t\n344\t| Component | Thread | Owns |\n345\t|---|---|---|\n346\t| UI, canvas paint | main | display |\n347\t| Frame encoder | worker | ring buffer (depth 3, I7) |\n348\t| QR decode pool | N workers | `VideoFrame` — MUST `close()` each or the pipeline stalls |\n349\t| GE decoder | 1 worker | the 72 KB matrix; single-owner, no sharing |\n350\t| OPFS writer | worker | `createSyncAccessHandle` is worker-only |\n351\t\n352\t**Backpressure policy:** if decode falls behind capture, camera frames are **dropped, not\n353\tqueued**. A queued frame is stale by the time it decodes, and queuing turns a throughput\n354\tproblem into a memory problem. Dropped frames are erasures, which the fountain code\n355\talready absorbs.\n356\t\n357\t### 6.3 Sender pipeline\n358\t\n359\t```\n360\tFile ──► [sample: compressible?] ──► CompressionStream ──► OPFS staging\n361\t  │            (D8, skip if not)                              │\n362\t  └──────────────── or straight through ─────────────────────┘\n363\t                                                              │\n364\t                                   cut into 192 KB blocks (D19)\n365\t                                                              │\n366\t                 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n367\t                 ▼                                            ▼\n368\t        beacon (D17/D21) every ~2 s          per block: slice → K=768 fragments\n369\t        filename · size · blockCount           → LT encode (d ≤ 64, D25)\n370\t        blockSize · L · K · hash · flags       → header → tile\n371\t                 │                                            │\n372\t                 └──────────────► frame mixer ◄───────────────┘\n373\t                                       │\n374\t                          ladder of 2–4 profiles (D16)\n375\t                                       │\n376\t                              DC-balance (D10) ──► canvas\n377\t                                       │\n378\t                     display at ≤ ½ measured camera fps (D9/D14)\n379\t```\n380\t\n381\tThe sender **dwells** on each block (§8.1), then advances, looping the file\n382\tcontinuously. It never terminates on its own — it cannot know when the receiver is done.\n383\t\n384\t> **Beacon clarification:** The beacon is a **packet** (distinguished by `PacketFlags.Beacon` in its header), not a separate frame. The \"frame mixer\" shown above combines beacon tiles (QR-encoded beacon packets) with payload tiles into the same displayed frames. This ensures minimal overhead: the sender emits beacon packets every ~2 seconds by replacing a few payload tiles in regular frames, rather than interrupting transmission with dedicated beacon frames.\n385\t\n386\t#### 6.3.1 Frames are generated on demand (D24)\n387\t\n388\tEvery arrow above is a **generator**, not an array.\n389\t\n390\t- **No finite frame set exists.** The LT encoder is rateless; how many frames a transfer\n391\t  needs depends on channel loss and is unknowable in advance.\n392\t- **One pass would not fit.** 4 GB ≈ 550,000 frames; as 1080p `ImageData` that is\n393\t  **4.2 TB**, ~55 GB even as PNGs.\n394\t- **On-demand is cheap.** ~0.29 ms per v15 tile (from 1.53 ms at v40, mask pinned) ×\n395\t  15 tiles × 15 fps ≈ **65 ms/sec, ~7% of one core**, plus ~2.3 ms/sec to render, plus\n396\t  **fountain XOR: 3.4 KB/packet at d ≤ 64 (D25) = 0.8 MB/s** at this geometry's\n397\t  **450 packets/s** (15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 15 fps, using the R2 nominal rung) —\n398\t  negligible, but only because of the cap. Uncapped it is 6.1 MB/s\n399\t  at K = 768, and was 91.8 MB/s at the old K = 16,384.\n400\t\n401\tBecause indices derive from a PRNG (D7), the sender is **stateless**: frame *N* generates\n402\tdirectly without replaying 1…*N*−1. That is what makes resume and repair nearly free.\n403\t\n404\t**Implementation:** worker generator → ring buffer (depth 3) → main thread paints via\n405\t`rAF`. Deeper buffering is wasted memory (I7).\n406\t\n407\t#### 6.3.2 Shape the code region to the CAMERA, not the screen\n408\t\n409\tMeasured, and worth ~4–5× on its own. The receiver's camera has a fixed aspect and a fixed\n410\tpixel count; the sender's screen has a different one. What matters is **camera px per module**\n411\t(§2), and that is set by how much of the capture the code region fills.\n412\t\n413\tA 1920×1080 landscape code region imaged by a portrait 1080×1920 capture yields **M = 0.5625** —\n414\tso 4 screen px/module is only 2.25 camera px/module, below the cliff. Rendering the *same*\n415\tpayload into a **portrait-shaped region** inverts this:\n416\t\n417\t| Code region on screen | M | Camera px/module @ 2 screen px | Tiles | QR cap/frame | Payload/frame |\n418\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n419\t| 1920×1080 (naive: fill the screen) | 0.56 | 1.13 — **far below cliff** | 15 | 8.8 KB | 7.5 KB |\n420\t| 1080×1080 square | 1.00 | 2.00 — below cliff | 9 | 5.3 KB | 4.5 KB |\n421\t| **540×960 portrait** | **2.00** | **4.00 — above cliff** | 15 | **8.8 KB** | **7.5 KB** |\n422\t\n423\tSame tile count and same bytes per frame as the naive layout, but *above* the cliff instead of\n424\tbelow it — so yield goes from roughly a fifth to near-total. **The sender MUST size the code\n425\tregion to the receiver's capture aspect, not to its own display.** Since there is no\n426\tback-channel, it cannot know that aspect: expose it as a user-visible setting (portrait /\n427\tlandscape receiver) **defaulting to portrait, which is how phones are held — and portrait is\n428\ta fully supported mode, not a degraded one.** The 540×960 portrait region above clears the\n429\tcliff (4.00 camera px/module) at the *same* 7.5 KB/frame payload as the naive landscape\n430\tlayout. **Phase 3's ≥ 20 KB/s gate MUST pass with the receiver held portrait, unaided** —\n431\tthat is the default, unassisted case, not a stretch goal.\n432\t\n433\t**Packets-per-tile basis.** The R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 60% of tiles in steady state per D18a)\n434\tcarries **2 packets per tile**. Each packet is 269 B (13-byte header + 256 B payload), so\n435\t2 packets = 538 B per tile, which fits within v16-L's 586 B capacity. The **user-visible payload**\n436\tis 15 tiles × 2 packets/tile × 256 B = **7,680 B/frame ≈ 7.5 KB/frame**, matching the table\n437\tabove (per §13.2, all throughput figures quote user-visible bytes, not wire bytes). The **8.8 KB/frame\n438\tQR capacity** is 15 tiles × 586 B (v16-L capacity). At 15 fps, this geometry delivers\n439\t**7.5 KB × 15 fps = 112.5 KB/s payload rate** (or ~113 KB/s) before fountain overhead\n440\tand erasure loss.\n441\t\n442\t**Two routes to the same M; landscape is a free bonus, not a requirement.** Physically holding\n443\tthe receiver in landscape puts the screen's long axis on the camera's long axis — **1.78×,\n444\tfree, and it does not require halving screen px/module the way the portrait-region layout\n445\tdoes** — so it is worth *offering* to a user willing to turn the phone. But the app MUST NOT\n446\tdepend on the user doing so: the sender-side portrait region (above) is the primary,\n447\talways-on path, and landscape is strictly an optional upgrade for extra margin on top of it.\n448\t\n449\tVerified negative: forcing the receiver's *OS* orientation does not help — sensor mapping\n450\tfollows the device body, not the UI. Since portrait is the supported default, this mostly\n451\tdoesn't matter; it only matters for the optional landscape upgrade, which needs a *physical*\n452\tturn (§11 `E-ORIENTATION`, reframed below as a tip, not a requirement).\n453\t\n454\t### 6.4 Receiver pipeline\n455\t\n456\t```\n457\tgetUserMedia ──► exposureCompensation:min (D14) ──► measure real fps (rVFC, ~1 s)\n458\t      │\n459\t      └──► requestVideoFrameCallback ──► MediaStreamTrackProcessor*\n460\t                                                │\n461\t                              ROI crop (conditional — see §6.4)\n462\t                                                │\n463\t                              ┌─────────────────┴──── Worker pool ────┐\n464\t                              ▼                                       ▼\n465\t                      zxing readBarcodes                     [Stage 2: split\n466\t                      (all symbols, .bytes)                   R/G/B, stretch, ×3]\n467\t                              │\n468\t                    header parse ──► fcrc ──► streamId lock ──► route by blockIndex\n469\t                              │                                        │\n470\t                     beacon? ──┴──► learn size/blocks/K/hash    payload ──► GE decoder\n471\t                                    (gates everything)\n472\t                                                        rank == K ──► write to OPFS\n473\t                                                                  ──► mark decode bitmap\n474\t                                                                  ──► verify hash (if manifest present)\n475\t                                                                  ──► mark verified bitmap\n476\t                                                                              │\n477\t                                            all blocks present & manifest decoded ──► verify all blocks\n478\t                                                                  ──► [decompress] ──► save\n479\t```\n480\t\n481\t\\* `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` is **Chromium-only**; `requestVideoFrameCallback` +\n482\t`drawImage` is the universal fallback and MUST be implemented (§16.3).\n483\t\n484\t**Block-layer working set: 264.0 KB** — 72.0 KB matrix + 192.0 KB block — flat regardless\n485\tof file size. This is *not* the whole-receiver figure; see I6a/I6b in §5.\n486\t\n487\tThree rules that are cheap to implement and expensive to omit:\n488\t\n489\t- **Measure fps, never trust it.** `getSettings()` reports 30/60 while the camera\n490\t  delivers 15.\n491\t- **Crop to ROI before decoding — but the 9× is conditional.** Measured 8.6× (56.9 → 6.6 ms)\n492\t  *when the code occupies part of the frame*. Once the grid fills the frame — which is what\n493\t  you want for camera px/module — **the ROI is the frame and the win evaporates** (69 ms).\n494\t  ROI is a recovery mechanism for being too far away, not a throughput optimisation at the\n495\t  right distance. **Except at high capture resolution**, where a tight quad-crop is what keeps\n496\t  camera px/module high *and* pixel count bounded at once — there it is load-bearing, and must\n497\t  be far tighter than the spike's 35%-margin version.\n498\t- **Select capture resolution deliberately — it is a first-class tunable.** Measured knee:\n499\t  720p → 100% erasure (1.5 camera px/module, nothing decodes); 1080p → best goodput; 4K →\n500\t  zero empty frames but 194 ms decode and 1.1 fps, net *worse*. Decode is O(pixels), so more\n501\t  resolution is not free. `getUserMedia` defaults are **not** adequate: a Pixel 6 defaults to\n502\t  1080 on the *short* edge.\n503\t- **Shape the code region to the camera, not the screen (sender-side, §6.3.2).**\n504\t- **Never offer a torch button.** It measured a 3.6× fps gain, which makes it tempting,\n505\t  but an LED on a glossy screen creates a specular hotspot that destroys a region of the\n506\t  frame. `exposureCompensation` gets the same mechanism without glare.\n507\t\n508\t### 6.5 Module layout and dependency pins\n509\t\n510\tCommitted in Phase 0 so \"where does this go?\" is not re-litigated eight phases running.\n511\tNote the layer boundaries of §6.1 and the thread boundaries of §6.2 are **not** the same,\n512\tso the tree separates them explicitly.\n513\t\n514\t```\n515\tsrc/\n516\t  core/                 # pure, no DOM, no workers — the testable heart\n517\t    fountain/           #   lt-encode.ts  ge-decode.ts  prng.ts  degree.ts\n518\t    block/              #   partition.ts  bitmap.ts  schedule.ts\n519\t    frame/              #   header.ts  beacon.ts  crc.ts  repair-code.ts\n520\t    hash/               #   block-hash.ts  stream-id.ts\n521\t  modulation/           # the swappable layer (§6.1)\n522\t    types.ts            #   the Modulation interface — the ONLY contract above\n523\t    qr-tiled/           #   stage 1: encode.ts  decode.ts  layout.ts  ladder.ts\n524\t    qr-colour/          #   stage 2\n525\t    grid/               #   stage 3\n526\t  workers/              # one file per thread role (§6.2)\n527\t    encode.worker.ts  decode.worker.ts  ge.worker.ts  opfs.worker.ts\n528\t  platform/             # every capability probe and fallback lives here\n529\t    camera.ts  storage.ts  wakelock.ts  share.ts  capabilities.ts\n530\t  ui/                   # role select, progress, coaching, pre-flight\n531\t  app.ts\n532\ttest/\n533\t  fixtures/             # conformance vectors (§14.3)\n534\t  degradation/          # synthetic blur/glare/tear generators\n535\tdocs/                   # plan, notes, research, sim\n536\t```\n537\t\n538\t**Rules.** `core/` MUST NOT import from `modulation/`, `workers/`, `platform/` or `ui/` —\n539\tit is the layer the property tests own. Nothing outside `modulation/` may reference QR\n540\t(D-modulation-swappable). Every browser capability check lives in\n541\t`platform/capabilities.ts`, never inline at a call site, so §16.1's platform matrix has\n542\texactly one implementation.\n543\t\n544\t**Dependency contract.** Exact-pinned, no ranges, no post-install scripts (gate G3).\n545\t\n546\t| Dependency | Pin | If unavailable |\n547\t|---|---|---|\n548\t| `zxing-wasm` | exact version + SRI on the `.wasm`. **MUST call `setZXingModuleOverrides({ locateFile })` pointing at a bundle-local, service-worker-precached `.wasm`.** See the warning below | Fatal on the receiver — surface `E-WASM-LOAD`; the sender still works |\n549\t| `node-qrcode` | exact version | Fatal on the sender; the receiver still works |\n550\t| `CompressionStream` | platform | Skip compression (D8 is already conditional) |\n551\t| `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` | platform | Fall back to `requestVideoFrameCallback` + `drawImage` — MUST be implemented, it is not Chromium-only |\n552\t| OPFS | platform | Refuse large files; cap at in-memory size and say so |\n553\t| Wake Lock | platform | Warn before a long transfer (`E-WAKELOCK-LOST`) |\n554\t\n555\t> ### ⚠️ `zxing-wasm` fetches its WASM from a CDN by default — this voids the entire premise\n556\t>\n557\t> Verified in the installed package: `dist/es/core-*.js` hard-codes\n558\t> `https://fastly.jsdelivr.net/npm/zxing-wasm@<ver>/dist/…` and fetches the `.wasm`\n559\t> **lazily on the first decode call**, not at page load. Shipping the default means the\n560\t> receiver:\n561\t>\n562\t> 1. makes a **third-party network request mid-session** — voiding T7, concept.md\n563\t>    constraint 1, and the README's \"provably no exfiltration\";\n564\t> 2. **fails completely in airplane mode** — i.e. in the flagship air-gapped use case (A8);\n565\t> 3. **executes remotely-fetched WASM** — precisely the supply-chain surface T5 exists for.\n566\t>\n567\t> The `.wasm` MUST be bundled, precached by the service worker, and located via\n568\t> `setZXingModuleOverrides`. §14.4's assertion covers this, and it is a **Phase 2 entry\n569\t> criterion** because Phase 2 is the first phase that loads a decoder.\n570\t\n571\t**Cross-origin isolation.** The pipeline uses transferable `VideoFrame`s and\n572\t`ArrayBuffer`s, **not** `SharedArrayBuffer` — so COOP/COEP headers are **not** required.\n573\tThis is deliberate: requiring them would constrain static hosting for no gain. Any future\n574\tuse of `SharedArrayBuffer` is a hosting decision, not just a code change.\n575\t\n576\t### 6.6 The luma-vs-colour disagreement, and how it is resolved\n577\t\n578\t| | `custom-codec-engineering.md` §7.2 | `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` §6.6 |\n579\t|---|---|---|\n580\t| Colour cell penalty under 4:2:0 | 2× linear (4× area) — **derived** | 1.25× linear (1.56× area) — **measured** |\n581\t| Verdict | luma-only wins ~1.95× | RGB-tripling wins **1.98×** |\n582\t\n583\tThe measured result is better founded and the mechanism convincing: **chroma decimation\n584\tis a low-pass filter, not a deletion.** A binary chroma pattern at 5 px/module presents\n585\t2.5 chroma samples per module — above Nyquist; at 4 px/module exactly 2.0, right at\n586\tNyquist, which is where the measurement breaks. The \"2× per axis\" rule over-corrects by\n587\trestoring the *original* sampling density rather than staying above Nyquist in the\n588\tdecimated grid.\n589\t\n590\tAlso weighing against luma-only: 8-level luma measured **unusable** under handheld blur\n591\t(21.2% symbol error at 5 px/cell) vs **0.00%** for saturated 8-colour at 4 px/cell; and\n592\t**libcimbar spends 2 of its 6 bits per cell on colour**, with its deprecated 8-colour\n593\tmode benchmarking *faster*.\n594\t\n595\t**Resolution (D11): neither document decides.** A calibration probe measures the device\n596\tat session start. Where the luma-side note is unambiguously right: **AWB warps colour in\n597\tthree non-monotonic dimensions** and cannot be locked on iOS, so a per-frame in-band\n598\tcolour reference is **not optional** for Stage 2.\n599\t\n600\t---\n601\t\n602\t## 7. Data model\n603\t\n604\t### 7.1 Payload packet header — 13 bytes\n605\t\n606\t| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |\n607\t|---|---|---|---|\n608\t| 0 | 1 | `magic_ver` | 4-bit magic + 4-bit wire version. Rejects foreign QR instantly. See §16.3 for version skew. |\n609\t| 1 | 1 | `flags` | packet type (payload/beacon), reserved |\n610\t| 2 | 4 | `streamId` | Identifies the **file**. Seeds the PRNG; receiver locks it on first sight. Derivation: §7.4 |\n611\t| 6 | 3 | `blockIndex` | 16.7 M blocks × 192 KB = **3.0 TB** addressable — beyond any practical transfer (1 TB is 117 days) |\n612\t| 9 | 3 | `seq` | Sequence **within the block**; with `streamId`+`blockIndex` derives the index set |\n613\t| 12 | 1 | `fcrc` | CRC-8 — rejects a mis-decode before it poisons the matrix |\n614\t\n615\t`K`, `L` and the index set remain **derived, never transmitted** (I3).\n616\t\n617\t**`fcrc` covers bytes 0–11 only — the header, NOT the payload.** This is deliberate: CRC-8\n618\tover 269 bytes would be weak anyway, and the header is what must be trusted before a packet\n619\tis routed to a block. But the consequence must be stated plainly:\n620\t\n621\t> **A packet whose header is intact and whose 256-byte payload is corrupted passes `fcrc`\n622\t> unconditionally and poisons the GE matrix.** `fcrc` is a routing guard, not an integrity\n623\t> check.\n624\t\n625\tPayload integrity therefore rests on exactly two things: QR's own Reed–Solomon (which makes\n626\tan undetected symbol error rare, but not impossible) and **the per-block hash (§7.6), which\n627\tis the sole application-layer check on payload bytes.** The manifest-based hash verification\n628\tensures corrupted blocks are detected before completion: a block that reaches rank K but fails\n629\tits hash is never surfaced to the user and triggers re-collection (`E-BLOCK-HASH`, §11, E12).\n630\tI9 enforces that unverified blocks written to OPFS are never exported or made visible to\n631\tthe user until the manifest arrives and verification succeeds. A test MUST corrupt a payload\n632\tbyte and assert the block hash catches it — corrupting only header bytes, as the current\n633\tsuite does, cannot detect this class at all.\n634\t\n635\t### 7.2 Beacon packet (D17/D21)\n636\t\n637\tEmitted every ~2 s at the most conservative profile. Everything the receiver needs before\n638\tit can interpret any payload packet:\n639\t\n640\t| Field | Size | Notes |\n641\t|---|---|---|\n642\t| `streamId` | 4 | Must match payload packets |\n643\t| `wireVersion` | 1 | Full version, not the 4-bit nibble |\n644\t| `fileSize` | 6 | 281 TB addressable — **MUST be bounds-checked** (§12, T1) |\n645\t| `blockSize`, `blockCount` | 3 + 3 | Yields K and the last block's short length |\n646\t| `fragmentLen` (L) | 2 | Fixed for the session (I1) |\n647\t| `degreeCap` | 1 | D25; receiver MUST use the same cap |\n648\t| `flags` | 1 | compressed / hash alg / colour profile |\n649\t| `blockHashLen` | 1 | Per-block hash truncation length |\n650\t| `wholeFileHash` | 32 | **Mandatory.** concept.md constraint 4 makes byte-exact reconstruction non-negotiable and names this as the verification. An earlier revision made it optional \"on very large files\" — i.e. dropped the guarantee exactly where E5 (source mutated during a 10-hour read) is most likely and the stakes are highest. Computed by streaming the reassembled file through an incremental WASM hasher (§3.3); the cost is one extra read, not one extra copy |\n651\t| `manifestHash` | 4 | **Mandatory.** CRC-32 of the manifest data (§7.6). Roots the cryptographic chain: **beacon → manifest → blocks → whole file**. Without this, a corrupted manifest packet would cause wrong block hashes, leading to infinite E12 failures with no error code or termination. The beacon already carries 32 bytes; adding 4 more is negligible. |\n652\t| `filename`, `mimeType` | var | Length-prefixed UTF-8, **sanitised** (§12, T2) |\n653\t\n654\tThe receiver shows \"acquiring…\" until its first beacon.\n655\t\n656\t### 7.6 The block-hash manifest — how per-block hashes reach the receiver\n657\t\n658\tI9, E12, §6.4, §8.3 and §7.4 all depend on per-block hashes, and §7.1 establishes they are\n659\tthe *only* application-layer check on payload bytes. Nothing in the wire format carried\n660\tthem: the 13-byte header has no room, and the beacon carries only `blockHashLen`.\n661\t\n662\t**A 4 GB file has 21,845 blocks. Even 4-byte hashes are 87 KB — far beyond a beacon.**\n663\t\n664\t**Resolution: hashes travel as a manifest, fountain-coded like any other block.**\n665\t\n666\t| Property | Value |\n667\t|---|---|\n668\t| Transport | A dedicated **manifest stream**, `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF`, distinguished by `PacketFlags.Manifest` |\n669\t| Contents | `blockCount × blockHashLen` truncated hashes, in block order |\n670\t| Integrity | **Mandatory validation via beacon's `manifestHash` field (§7.2)**. The beacon carries a 4-byte CRC-32 of the manifest data. After decoding the manifest, the receiver MUST compute its CRC-32 and compare against the beacon's `manifestHash`. A mismatch indicates corruption and MUST cause the manifest to be discarded and re-decoded. This prevents infinite E12 failures from corrupted manifest data. |\n671\t| `blockHashLen` | **4 bytes.** Per-block false accept 2⁻³², ~5×10⁻⁶ across 21,845 blocks — comfortably below the whole-file hash's job |\n672\t| Coding | **Fixed K=768 multi-block stream** — `blockCount_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)`, same LT encoder, same GE decoder. Each manifest block is fountain-coded independently, inheriting the flat-cost property. |\n673\t| Cadence | Interleaved with payload on the same schedule as the beacon (D17), so a late joiner acquires it without waiting a pass |\n674\t| Before it arrives | Completed blocks are written to OPFS but tracked separately from verified blocks (two-bitmap system: `complete` for decoded, `writtenBlocks` for written). They are verified retroactively once the manifest decodes. The receiver reports \"verifying…\" rather than claiming completion. **Critical: blocks written before verification are NEVER surfaced to the user or exported until their hash is verified (I9).** |\n675\t\n676\t**Why not append the hash to each block's payload:** it would make the payload\n677\t`blockSize + 4`, breaking `blockSize = K·L` and therefore D19's entire arithmetic and G7.\n678\t\n679\t**Sizing sanity:** 21,845 blocks × 4 B = 87 KB at 4 GB ⇒ `blockCount_manifest` = 1 (one block). At 100 GB (546,125 blocks): 2.1 MB ⇒ 11 blocks. At 1 TB (5.46M blocks): 21 MB ⇒ 110 blocks. Each block decodes at K=768 (72 KB matrix), so memory stays bounded regardless of file size — flat-cost by design.\n680\t\n681\t**Why the manifest hash is mandatory:** Without it, a single flipped byte in the manifest\n682\tpacket would yield wrong hashes for hundreds of blocks. Those blocks would fail E12 forever\n683\t— re-collect, fail, re-collect — with no error code and no termination. The manifest hash\n684\tdetects this corruption immediately and forces re-decode of the manifest.\n685\t\n686\t### 7.3 Session state\n687\t\n688\t```ts\n689\ttype SendSession = {\n690\t  source: File;\n691\t  staging: FileSystemFileHandle | null;   // compressed copy (D8) — MUST be wiped\n692\t  streamId: number;\n693\t  blockSize: number; blockCount: number;\n694\t  readonly fragmentLen: number;           // L — I1\n695\t  readonly K: number;                     // D26\n696\t  cursor: { blockIndex: number; seq: number };\n697\t  dwellPackets: number;                   // §8.1\n698\t};\n699\t\n700\ttype RecvSession = {\n701\t  streamId: number | null;                // locked on first valid header\n702\t  meta: BeaconMeta | null;                // gates everything\n703\t  complete: Uint8Array;                   // block bitmap — tracks decoded blocks\n704\t  writtenBlocks: Uint8Array;              // bitmap tracking blocks written to OPFS\n705\t  active: { blockIndex: number; pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5 — payload block GE context\n706\t  manifestActive: { pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5 — manifest block GE context\n707\t  manifest: BlockHashManifest | null;    // §7.6 — persisted for resume\n708\t  out: FileSystemWritableFileStream;      // OPFS\n709\t  stats: { fps: number; cameraPxPerModule: number; packetsPerSec: number; eta: number };\n710\t};\n711\t```\n712\t\n713\t**Two-bitmap system:** `complete` tracks blocks that have been fountain-decoded; `writtenBlocks` tracks blocks that have been written to OPFS. These separate because blocks may be decoded before their hashes arrive (§7.6), and they must not be surfaced to the user until verified.\n714\t\n715\tPartial state for a block the sender has moved past is **discarded, not persisted** — a\n716\tbadly damaged block rarely half-completes usefully, and persisting it would defeat I6.\n717\tThe bitmap is tiny: 4 GB / 192 KB = 21,845 blocks = **2.7 KB**.\n718\t\n719\t### 7.4 `streamId` derivation\n720\t\n721\tLoad-bearing: D22 resume requires that re-selecting the same file reproduces the same\n722\t`streamId`, and §3.3 says a full multi-GB hash is not free.\n723\t\n724\t**Derivation (sender):**\n725\t\n726\t```\n727\tstreamId = CRC32( fileSize ‖ first 64 KB ‖ middle 64 KB ‖ last 64 KB ‖ lastModified )\n728\t```\n729\t\n730\tThree sampled windows plus size and mtime. Costs ~200 KB of reads regardless of file\n731\tsize, so it is instant even for 4 TB.\n732\t\n733\t**What this buys and what it does not:**\n734\t\n735\t- ✅ Same file re-selected → same `streamId` → resume works.\n736\t- ✅ Different files → different `streamId` with overwhelming probability.\n737\t- ⚠️ A file edited **only in the middle**, keeping size and mtime, collides. Mitigated by\n738\t  including `lastModified`, and by per-block hashes catching the mismatch at block level.\n739\t- ⚠️ This is **not** a content-integrity hash. The whole-file hash (§7.2) is, and is\n740\t  optional. `streamId` is an *identifier*.\n741\t\n742\tDeliberately **not** `crc32(payload)` — the research's original design — because the\n743\tblock layer made a full-payload pass unaffordable.\n744\t\n745\t### 7.5 Repair code format (§8.2)\n746\t\n747\tA human types this, so it must be short, unambiguous, and self-checking.\n748\t\n749\t```\n750\tSF1-<streamId36>-<ranges36>-<check>\n751\t```\n752\t\n753\t- **Alphabet:** Crockford base32 (no I/L/O/U — removes the common misreadings).\n754\t- **`ranges`:** run-length encoded missing-block set. Contiguous runs are the common case\n755\t  because misses cluster (the user looked away).\n756\t- **`check`:** 2 characters, CRC-8 over the decoded body. A mistyped code MUST be\n757\t  rejected, never acted on — acting on a corrupted range wastes hours.\n758\t- **Length bound:** if the encoded form exceeds **48 characters**, the receiver MUST\n759\t  instead offer a QR containing the same payload (which the sender's camera reads, or the\n760\t  user photographs), and say so. A 100 GB file with scattered misses can exceed any\n761\t  reasonable typing length, and silently truncating the set would be a correctness bug.\n762\t\n763\t---\n764\t\n765\t## 8. Behaviour at gigabyte scale\n766\t\n767\t### 8.1 Block scheduling and the dwell budget\n768\t\n769\tThe sender does not know which blocks the receiver has, so it dwells on each block for\n770\t`dwellPackets`, then advances, looping the file continuously.\n771\t\n772\t**Dwell must survive the top of the assumed erasure band.** An earlier revision paired\n773\tdwell 1.4 K with a 20–30% band, which failed at the top of its own band — at 30%\n774\terasure, 1.4 K delivers 0.98 K against the ~1.02 K needed, so **every block missed its\n775\tfirst pass**, each costing a full extra pass.\n776\t\n777\tThe fix is to raise dwell, **not** to narrow the band. Narrowing it (a briefly-adopted\n778\tmistake) contradicts the evidence base, which specifies 20–30% and warns that driving\n779\terasure lower means the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused.\n780\t\n781\t| dwell | 20% erasure | 25% | **30%** | needed |\n782\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n783\t| 1.4 K | 1.120 K | 1.050 K | **0.980 K ❌** | ~1.02 K |\n784\t| **1.6 K** | 1.280 K | 1.200 K | **1.120 K ✅** | ~1.02 K |\n785\t\n786\t- **dwell = 1.6 × K** (default; tunable)\n787\t- **assumed band = 20–30%** (D18c) — an assumption, not a controlled target\n788\t\n789\tA test MUST assert `dwell × (1 − erasure_max) ≥ 1.12`, matching §13.1's +12% p99\n790\toverhead budget, so dwell and the band cannot drift apart again.\n791\t\n792\t**When real erasure exceeds 30%** — which nothing in v1 can detect (D18a) — blocks miss\n793\tand the **repair code (§8.2) is the recovery path**, not a tighter loop. This is the\n794\tdesigned answer, not a gap.\n795\t\n796\t**Dwell is a standing ~60% overhead.** The sender always emits 1.6× what a block needs,\n797\twhatever the channel. §13.1's throughput budgets are stated **after** this factor —\n798\tthey are goodput, not wire rate.\n799\t\n800\t### 8.2 Human-mediated repair — the cheap back-channel\n801\t\n802\tThe receiver knows exactly which blocks it lacks. The user reads a code off one screen and\n803\ttypes it into the other:\n804\t\n805\t> **Receiver:** \"Missing 3 blocks. Repair code: `SF1-K7F2M9-3B-X4`\"\n806\t> **Sender:** [paste] → transmits only those blocks\n807\t\n808\tTurns a multi-hour extra pass into a sub-minute repair, needs no second camera and no\n809\tgeometry constraints, and is what makes small blocks (§3.4) affordable. Format: §7.5.\n810\t\n811\t### 8.3 Resume (D22)\n812\t\n813\tThe receiver persists `{streamId, meta, complete, writtenBlocks, manifest}` plus the OPFS output after every completed\n814\tblock. On reload it offers to resume. At 2.7 KB per 4 GB for the bitmaps this is nearly free; the manifest adds\n815\t87 KB for a 4 GB file (21,845 blocks × 4-byte hashes). **The manifest MUST be persisted** — without it,\n816\tresume cannot re-verify blocks, and a reload during the ~12 minute manifest acquisition window would lose\n817\tall received blocks.\n818\t\n819\tThe sender is stateless across restarts by construction (D24) **when compression is disabled** —\n820\tit needs only the same file and the same `streamId` (§7.4). **With compression enabled, resume is\n821\tNOT supported** — see `docs/notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md` for the full analysis,\n822\t`docs/notes/bf-3k90-compression-resume-solution-evaluation.md` for the solution evaluation,\n823\tand `notes/bf-2w1a.md` for validation and test coverage.\n824\tThe short version: `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after\n825\tstaging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state.\n826\tThe beacon carries a `ResumeDisabled` flag (beacon `flags` field) when compression is on;\n827\tthe receiver uses this flag to suppress resume UI and prevent persisting resume tokens.\n828\tThis preserves the T4 privacy requirement (staging is still wiped on startup) while preventing\n829\tsilent corruption.\n830\t\n831\t**On resume the receiver MUST re-verify block hashes** rather than trusting the bitmap, in\n832\tcase OPFS was corrupted or the file was touched externally. This requires the manifest to be\n833\tpersisted alongside the bitmap.\n834\t\n835\t**Pre-manifest reload behavior:** If the receiver is reloaded before the manifest arrives\n836\t(e.g., during the ~12 minute acquisition window for a 4 GB file at the beacon's ~2 s cadence),\n837\tthe persisted bitmap preserves which blocks were decoded, and the written blocks remain in OPFS.\n838\tThe `writtenBlocks` bitmap is reset on resume, and blocks are re-verified once the manifest arrives.\n839\tThis prevents losing all received blocks during the manifest acquisition window.\n840\t\n841\t### 8.4 Storage limits\n842\t\n843\t| Platform | Practical quota |\n844\t|---|---|\n845\t| Chrome / Edge desktop | ~60% of free disk — multi-GB fine |\n846\t| Firefox | ~10% of disk (capped ~10 GB) |\n847\t| **Safari / iOS** | **~1 GB** before prompting; expandable but user-gated |\n848\t\n849\t**Multi-GB reception is a desktop-Chromium story.** The app MUST query\n850\t`navigator.storage.estimate()` up front and refuse clearly (§13.1) rather than failing at\n851\thour 9. With compression on, staging needs the compressed size *plus* the output.\n852\t\n853\t---\n854\t\n855\t## 9. Acceptance scenarios\n856\t\n857\tNamed, independently verifiable, with explicit pass **and fail** criteria. \"Fail\" means\n858\tstop and reconsider the design, not retry.\n859\t\n860\t| # | Scenario | Setup | Action | Pass | Fail |\n861\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n862\t| **A1** | Small file, ideal conditions | Laptop (1080p, 50% brightness min) → Pixel-class phone, 30 cm, office lighting (~300 lux), tripod | Send a 1 MB binary file (random bytes, incompressible) | Byte-identical output; ≥ 20 KB/s sustained; completes in ≤ 60 s | < 10 KB/s, or any byte differs |\n863\t| **A1-lite** | Byte-exactness on two real devices | Two real devices (any configuration) | Send any file | Byte-identical output | Any byte differs |\n864\t| **A2** | Handheld, realistic | As A1 but handheld, receiver held **portrait** (the default, unassisted grip — §6.3.2) | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≥ 10 KB/s | Does not complete in 5 min |\n865\t| **A3** | Phone → phone | Two phones, 15 cm, handheld | Send 100 KB | Byte-identical; completes in ≤ 5 min | Does not complete — triggers §18 R4 |\n866\t| **A4** | Lossy channel | A1 setup; camera deliberately occluded 30% of the time in 2-second bursts | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≤ 1.6× the A1 frame count | > 3× A1 frame count (fountain code is not delivering) |\n867\t| **A5** | Large file, memory flat | Desktop Chromium, synthetic 4 GB stream, headless block layer | Full encode→decode at the block layer | Byte-identical; peak heap ≤ 1 MB (I6a); no growth trend across 21,800 blocks | Any monotonic memory growth |\n868\t| **A6** | Resume | A1 setup, 10 MB file | Reload the receiver tab at ~50% | Offers resume; completes; byte-identical | Restarts from zero, or completes with wrong bytes |\n869\t| **A7** | Repair | A1 setup, 10 MB file, 5 blocks deliberately dropped | Enter the repair code on the sender | Only the missing blocks retransmit; completes in < 60 s | Full pass required |\n870\t| **A8** | Offline | Both devices in airplane mode, app previously loaded | Full A1 transfer | Completes normally | Any network request attempted (asserted by CI, §14.4) |\n871\t| **A9** | Wrong stream | Two senders visible in frame | Receiver points at both | Locks one `streamId`, ignores the other, says so | Mixes packets from both |\n872\t| **A10** | Hostile beacon | Crafted beacon declaring `fileSize` = 281 TB | Receiver parses it | Refuses with `E-META-BOUNDS`; no allocation attempted | Allocates or crashes |\n873\t\n874\t**Adoption metrics are deliberately absent.** With no backend and no telemetry there is no\n875\tway to measure them, and the ledger consciously cut the voluntary-benchmark idea. This is a\n876\tstated limitation, not an oversight — see §18 R8.\n877\t\n878\t---\n879\t\n880\t## 10. Edge case catalog\n881\t\n882\t| # | Case | Resolution |\n883\t|---|---|---|\n884\t| E1 | **Zero-byte file** | Reject at selection with a clear message. `K = 0` is undefined. |\n885\t| E2 | **File smaller than one fragment** (< 256 B) | Pad to one fragment; `K = 1`; the fountain code degenerates to repetition, which is correct. Research specifies a `K < 8` guard — adopt it: below 8 fragments, send plain repetition, no LT. **Repetition is derived per-block** (not signalled): both encoder and decoder derive `repetition = (k < MIN_LT_K)` from the block's K using the shared per-block derivation E3a already mandates. A session-wide flag would force repetition on all 21,845 blocks or none; per-block derivation allows the last block (K=1-7) to use repetition while all other blocks (K=768) use LT. |\n886\t| E3a | **The last block is short** — its K is `ceil(lastLen / L)`, not 768. Both sides derive K per block, and D7's PRNG is seeded with it. A mismatch produces wrong index sets, so the block never decodes and nothing says why. | Derive per-block K from `(blockIndex, blockSize, fileSize)` in **one shared function** used by both encoder and decoder; conformance vector covers the last block explicitly. |\n887\t| E3b | **`blockCount == 1`** | Normal path; no special case, but tested explicitly since off-by-one in block iteration is likely. |\n888\t| E4 | **Incompressible input where deflate expands it** | D8 samples first; if the sample ratio > 0.92, skip compression. If compression still expands, discard the staging file and send raw. |\n889\t| E5 | **Source file changes mid-transfer** | A 10-hour read of a live `File` handle is the *normal* case. Re-check `file.size` and `lastModified` before each block read; on mismatch abort with `E-SOURCE-CHANGED`. Emitting blocks from two versions would produce a file that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours. |\n890\t| E6 | **Duplicate packet arrives** | GE reduces it to a zero row; contributes nothing, costs one reduction. No special handling. |\n891\t| E7 | **Two senders in frame** | `streamId` lock (A9); packets from the unlocked stream are discarded and surfaced as `E-FOREIGN-STREAM`. |\n892\t| E8 | **Tab backgrounded on the sender** | `rAF` stops in a background tab, so a 10-hour transfer silently halts. Wake Lock does **not** cover this. Detect via `visibilitychange` and warn loudly; the transfer is paused, not failed. |\n893\t| E9 | **Camera permission revoked mid-run** | Pause, preserve the bitmap, prompt for re-grant. Never discard collected blocks. |\n894\t| E10 | **OPFS quota exhausted mid-transfer** | Stop, keep completed blocks, export a partial file plus a manifest of what is missing. Never silently truncate. **The kept partial artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n895\t| E11 | **Abandoned staging file** | Sender-side staging keyed by `streamId`; on startup, reap staging files with no active session. Also a privacy requirement (§12, T4a). |\n896\t| E12 | **Block hash verification fails** | After manifest arrives, block hash verification fails. Clear the verified bitmap bit, re-collect the block. Emit `E-BLOCK-HASH`. Block may already be written to OPFS but is never surfaced until verified (I9). This is the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) and MUST be implemented — at GB scale a silent re-do costs hours. |\n897\t| E13 | **Whole-file hash fails after all blocks pass** | Indicates E5 or a block-hash collision. Report `E-FILE-HASH`; keep the output and label it unverified rather than deleting hours of work. |\n898\t| E14 | **Filename with path separators or control bytes** | Sanitise on export (§12, T2). Never write an attacker-chosen path. |\n899\t| E15 | **Decompression fails at the end** | All blocks verified but the gzip stream is invalid → `E-DECOMPRESS`; keep the compressed artefact so nothing is lost. **The kept artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n900\t| E16 | **Worker crash mid-block** | Restart the worker, discard the active block only, keep the bitmap. |\n901\t| E17a | **Sender-side thermal throttling** | Observed: the bench laptop decayed 6.7 → 2.4 fps over two minutes. Locally observable, so D18b's local step-down applies. |\n902\t| E17b | **Receiver-side thermal throttling** | Observed at **70 °C / throttling threshold within 20–30 minutes**. D18a's rule bites: fps decline is a *receiver* observation, the ladder is a *sender* control, and there is no back-channel — so \"step the ladder down\" is **structurally impossible** here. Mitigate locally instead: **duty-cycle (D27)** and drop decode resolution. |\n903\t| E18 | **Resume offered for a file the user no longer has** (sender side) | `streamId` mismatch on re-selection → offer a fresh transfer, do not silently restart. |\n904\t\n905\t---\n906\t\n907\t## 11. Error taxonomy\n908\t\n909\tEvery distinguishable condition gets a stable code and one user-facing sentence. Defined\n910\tnow, before Phase 5 designs any UI — after that, taxonomies get retrofitted to screens.\n911\t\n912\t**Optical / acquisition** (the stall detector's job, `bf-5vm`):\n913\t\n914\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n915\t|---|---|---|\n916\t| `E-NO-SIGNAL` | No decodable tiles at all | \"Point the camera at the sending screen.\" |\n917\t| `E-TOO-FAR` | **camera** px/module < 4 (§2) | \"Move closer — the code is too small to read.\" |\n918\t| `E-TOO-CLOSE` | Symbol exceeds frame, or below min focus | \"Move back a little.\" |\n919\t| `E-BLUR` | Sharpness metric below threshold | \"Hold steady.\" |\n920\t| `E-DARK` | Insufficient exposure | \"Too dark — raise the sender's screen brightness.\" |\n921\t| `E-GLARE` | Saturated region over the code | \"Tilt to avoid the reflection.\" |\n922\t| `E-FOCUS-HUNT` | Focus oscillating | \"Tap the screen to lock focus.\" |\n923\t| `E-ORIENTATION` | Detected capture aspect doesn't match the sender's configured setting (§6.3.2) — e.g. sender is shaping the code for landscape but the receiver is held portrait | \"This app works fine held normally — but if you'd like more margin, match the orientation setting on the sending device, or turn the phone sideways.\" (tip, not a blocker — portrait is fully supported) |\n924\t| `E-SENDER-STALLED` | Identical frames repeating | \"The sending device seems paused.\" |\n925\t| `E-TORN` | Torn-frame rate high | \"Lower the sender's frame rate.\" |\n926\t\n927\t**Protocol:**\n928\t\n929\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n930\t|---|---|---|---|\n931\t| `E-FOREIGN-STREAM` | Different `streamId` (E7) | \"That's a different file — ignoring it.\" | automatic, informational |\n932\t| `E-VERSION` | Unknown `magic_ver` (§16.3) | \"The sending device is running version X; this one is Y. Update both.\" | user must update |\n933\t| `E-META-BOUNDS` | Beacon field out of bounds (T1) | \"That transmission looks malformed and was rejected.\" | automatic, refuse |\n934\t| `E-MANIFEST-CORRUPT` | Manifest CRC validation failed (§7.6) | \"The block manifest is corrupted and is being re-decoded.\" | automatic retry |\n935\t| `E-MANIFEST-MISSING` | Manifest never arrived (§7.6) | \"Waiting for block manifest to verify received chunks.\" | wait or request repair |\n936\t| `E-MANIFEST-DECODE` | Manifest fountain decode failed (§7.6) | \"Could not decode the block manifest. Retrying...\" | automatic retry |\n937\t| `E-MANIFEST-LIVELOCK` | E12 livelock detected, manifest corrupted (bf-5fm) | \"Multiple chunks failed verification — the manifest appears corrupted. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n938\t| `E-BLOCK-HASH` | Rank K reached, hash failed (E12) | \"A chunk arrived corrupted and is being re-collected.\" | automatic retry |\n939\t| `E-BLOCK-RETRY-EXCEEDED` | Block retry limit exceeded (E12 livelock, bf-5fm) | \"A chunk has failed verification too many times. Re-decoding manifest...\" | re-decode manifest |\n940\t| `E-K-OVERFLOW` | Sender K exceeds receiver's maximum (D26) | \"Sender's chunk size is too large for this device. Use a smaller file or a more powerful receiver.\" | refuse, user adjusts |\n941\t| `E-REPAIR-BOUNDS` | Repair code references blocks beyond file (§8.2) | \"That repair code refers to chunks that don't exist. Check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n942\t| `E-REPAIR-CODE` | Repair code checksum failed | \"That repair code doesn't look right — check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n943\t| `E-FILE-HASH` | Whole-file hash failed (E13) | \"The file is complete but failed its final check — saved as unverified.\" | keep output, warn |\n944\t| `E-WASM-LOAD` | Decoder failed to load | \"The scanner failed to start. Reload the page.\" | user reloads |\n945\t\n946\t**Status codes** (informational, not errors):\n947\t\n948\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n949\t|---|---|---|\n950\t| `E-VERIFYING` | Verifying blocks against manifest (§7.6) | \"Verifying received chunks against manifest...\" |\n951\t\n952\t**Local / resource:**\n953\t\n954\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n955\t|---|---|---|---|\n956\t| `E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT` | Not enough storage (§13.1) | \"Not enough free space: this needs X, you have Y.\" | user frees space |\n957\t| `E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED` | Ran out mid-transfer (E10) | \"Out of space. Saved what arrived — X of Y chunks.\" | partial export |\n958\t| `E-SOURCE-CHANGED` | Source mutated (E5) | \"The file changed while sending. Start again to avoid a corrupt copy.\" | restart required |\n959\t| `E-BACKGROUNDED` | Sender tab backgrounded (E8) | \"Sending paused — keep this tab visible.\" | auto-resume on focus |\n960\t| `E-CAMERA-LOST` | Permission revoked (E9) | \"Camera access ended. Your progress is saved.\" | re-grant, resume |\n961\t| `E-WAKELOCK-LOST` | Screen may sleep | \"The screen may turn off. Adjust your sleep settings.\" | user acts |\n962\t| `E-DECOMPRESS` | Decompression failed (E15) | \"Everything arrived but couldn't be unpacked. The raw data was kept.\" | keep artefact |\n963\t\n964\t---\n965\t\n966\t## 12. Threat model\n967\t\n968\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n969\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n970\t\n971\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n972\t|---|---|---|---|\n973\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `fileSize` (281 TB), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `fileSize` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n974\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n975\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `fileSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n976\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n977\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The output **is** the deliverable — it cannot be deleted immediately. For sensitive files (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) indefinite storage is exposure. | **Mitigated.** Implement a deletion lifecycle: (1) delete after successful `share()`/`save()`; (2) reap orphaned outputs on startup; (3) warn before keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15); (4) provide a user-visible delete control. Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest. | integration: assert receiver OPFS empty after successful save; reap deletes orphans; UI has delete control; warning shown for partial artefacts |\n978\t| **T5** | **Supply chain.** The security claim depends on the bundle being what was audited. | **Partially mitigated.** `bf-13h` covers the output half (version footer + published hash). The input half — pinned dependency versions, WASM integrity, no post-install scripts — is a Phase 0 requirement (§14.5). | G3: lockfile diff + SRI check in CI |\n979\t| **T6** | **Shoulder-surfing / filming.** The optical channel is uniquely exposed: anyone with a camera in the room captures the same stream. | **Accepted for v1, consciously.** concept.md scopes encryption as a non-goal; §19 Q10 keeps it live. The app MUST NOT claim confidentiality it does not provide — the UI should say the transmission is visible to anyone who can see the screen. | none — accepted, not mitigated |\n980\t| **T7** | **No telemetry, by construction.** | **Committed.** The app makes **zero** network requests after load. Enforced by CI (§14.4) and by A8. This is a stronger and more checkable claim than a privacy policy. | §14.4 network assertion + A8 |\n981\t\n982\t**Out of scope for v1, stated:** authenticating the *sender* (no PKI, no trust anchor); a\n983\tmalicious *receiver* (it only gets what it is shown); side-channels other than the optical\n984\tone; physical device compromise.\n985\t\n986\t---\n987\t\n988\t## 13. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n989\t\n990\t### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n991\t\n992\t§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n993\t\n994\t**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n995\t- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n996\t- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n997\t- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n998\t\n999\tThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n1000\t**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). After fountain (+12%) and 30% erasure,\n1001\tnet goodput is **~70 KB/s** — well above the 20 KB/s budget.\n1002\t\n1003\t| Budget | Value | Gate |\n1004\t|---|---|---|\n1005\t| Throughput, A1 reference setup | **≥ 20 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3 |\n1006\t| Throughput, A3 phone→phone | **≥ 3 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3; miss triggers §18 R4 |\n1007\t| Block-layer working set | **≤ 1 MB**, any file size (I6a) | Phase 1 |\n1008\t| Whole-receiver peak | **≤ 64 MB**, ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s (I6b) | Phase 3 |\n1009\t| GE sustained XOR need | **≤ 200 MB/s** at the fastest supported stage (modelled 114.6 MB/s, 1.74× margin) — **measured 3,260 MB/s desktop / ~815 MB/s est. phone; the budget was ~16× pessimistic.** R1 provisionally closed, pending an on-device run *while thermally throttled* | Phase 1 + G7 |\n1010\t| Per-camera-frame decode | **≤ 60 ms** p99 (leaves headroom at 15 fps) — **measured 67–69 ms p50 full-frame, 194 ms at 4K, 6.6 ms with a tight ROI. p50 already exceeds the p99 budget**; the fixes (worker pool §6.2, tight ROI §6.4) are unimplemented, so this is violated by the instrument, not yet by the design | Phase 3 |\n1011\t| Encode + render per frame | **≤ 20 ms** p99 — **measured ~150 ms** (6.7 fps against 12 requested) on a 2015 laptop with D4's pinned mask unimplemented | Phase 3 |\n1012\t| Time-to-first-packet after aim | **≤ 3 s** p50 | Phase 5 |\n1013\t| Reception overhead vs K | **≤ +5%** mean, **≤ +12%** p99 (measured: +2.97% / +4.2%) | Phase 1, `sim/` |\n1014\t| **Sustained operation duration** | **≥ 20 min** sustained throughput within **30% of initial rate** on target phone (Pixel 6-class) without active cooling. This is the **minimum viable duration** before R11's thermal throttling mitigation (duty-cycle reduction) must engage. The system is not required to avoid throttling indefinitely—only to (a) sustain long enough for practical use and (b) detect and surface throttling when it occurs (E17b, D27). | Phase 3; validated by T-long-run |\n1015\t| **Warn threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 30 min** → explicit confirm | Phase 4 |\n1016\t| **Refuse threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 24 h**, or quota insufficient → refuse with an override | Phase 4 |\n1017\t\n1018\t### 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n1019\t\n1020\tEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n1021\t\n1022\t| Parameter | Reference value |\n1023\t|---|---|\n1024\t| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes. With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n1025\t| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n1026\t| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n1027\t| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n1028\t| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n1029\t| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n1030\t| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n1031\t| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n1032\t| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n1033\t\n1034\t**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\n1035\ta 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\n1036\tto handheld numbers.\n1037\t\n1038\t---\n1039\t\n1040\t## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n1041\t\n1042\t### 14.1 Tiers\n1043\t\n1044\t| Tier | What | Runs |\n1045\t|---|---|---|\n1046\t| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n1047\t| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n1048\t| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. Objective\n\n> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n>\n> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n\n- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n\n### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n\nMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\ndesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\nBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n\n| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n\n> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n> one would overstate throughput.\n\n**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\nand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n\n1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Glossary\n\nSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\nplan they mean exactly this:\n\n| Term | Meaning here |\n|---|---|\n| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n| **Beacon** | A special **packet** carrying file-level metadata instead of payload. Beacon packets are encoded into tiles and mixed into display frames by the frame mixer (D17, §7.2). |\n| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n\n---\n\n## 3. What multi-gigabyte breaks, and the fix\n\nFour assumptions in the pre-multi-GB design do not survive contact with a 4 GB file.\n\n### 3.1 The fountain decoder does not scale — in TIME, not memory\n\nThis is the correction the plan review surfaced, and it matters because the first\nversion of this section got it half right.\n\nD5 chose an LT code with a **Gaussian elimination** decoder, verified at\n[`sim/`](../research/sim/). GE costs O(K²) in *memory* and O(K³) in *bit operations*.\nThe original block-layer decision sized K from the memory term alone and concluded 4 MB\nblocks (K = 16,384) were fine because the coefficient matrix is only 32 MB.\n\n**The memory term was never the binding constraint. Time is.**\n\nEach arriving packet is reduced against up to `rank` stored pivot rows; each row\noperation XORs the coefficient mask (K/8 bytes) *and* the payload (L bytes). Reaching\nfull rank costs `W = 2 · (K²/2) · (K/8 + L) = K² · (K/8 + L)` bytes of memory traffic,\nand the block only lasts `K·L / R` seconds at wire rate R — so the decoder must\n**sustain**:\n\n```\nrequired = W / (K·L/R) = K · (K/8 + L) · R / L    bytes/sec\n```\n\n> The leading factor is **1, not 2** — the 2 and the /2 in `W` cancel. A previous\n> revision of this section printed `2 · K · (K/8 + L) · R / L` and was 2× too\n> pessimistic in every derived figure. Gate **G7** now diffs this section against the\n> model so the class of error cannot recur.\n\nAll figures below are emitted by\n[`sim/ge_cost_model.py`](../research/sim/ge_cost_model.py) — this section quotes the\nmodel rather than reasoning beside it. **All rows at Stage 1 (R = 30 KB/s)**, so they\nare comparable:\n\n| K | L | Block | Matrix | Work/block | Sustained need | |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1,000 | 1260 | 1.2 MB | 122.1 KB | 1.3 GB | 33.8 MB/s | research baseline |\n| 1,500 | 1260 | 1.8 MB | 274.7 KB | 3.0 GB | 52.9 MB/s | research partitioning ceiling |\n| 4,000 | 1260 | 4.8 MB | 1.9 MB | 26.2 GB | 171.6 MB/s | research called this **\"too slow\"** |\n| **16,384** | **256** | **4.0 MB** | **32.0 MB** | **576.0 GB** | **4.5 GB/s** | **23× over budget** |\n\nThe plan's own evidence base\n([`fountain-codes-and-protocol.md`](../research/fountain-codes-and-protocol.md) §2.6)\nstates: *\"Cost scales as K², so it must be bounded. At K = 4000 the decode work is ~16×\nthat of K = 1000 (~6 GB of XOR) — too slow\"* and recommends *\"source-block partitioning\nabove K ≈ 1500\"*. **K = 16,384 was 11× past that ceiling.**\n\nIt was worse than a simple overshoot: shrinking L to 256 B to fit small tiles made the\nmask term (K/8 = 2048 B) dominate the payload term (256 B) by 8×, so the decode problem\ngot *harder* as a side effect of a decision made for a different reason.\n\n**Two further findings from the model:**\n\n- **A faster wire rate makes decode harder** — same work, less time to do it. So K MUST\n  be sized for the *fastest* stage we intend to reach (Stage 3, 106 KB/s), not the\n  slowest. This is counterintuitive and is why the original error was easy to make.\n- **The sender's cost was unbudgeted too.** §6.3.1 counted QR encode and render but not\n  the fountain XOR. At uncapped harmonic degree and K = 16,384 that is 398 KB of XOR\n  per packet — **91.8 MB/s** at the old 225 packets/s (1 packet/tile), or **183.6 MB/s**\n  at the adopted 450 packets/s (2 packets/tile at R2 nominal), on top of everything\n  else. Hence D25.\n\n**Fix — D19:** K = **768**, L = **256 B**, block = **192.0 KB**.\n\n| | Was | Now |\n|---|---|---|\n| K | 16,384 | **768** |\n| L | 256 B | **256 B** (unchanged — see §3.1.1) |\n| Block | 4 MB | **192.0 KB** |\n| GE matrix | 32.0 MB | **72.0 KB** |\n| Block-layer working set | ~36 MB (claimed) | **264.0 KB** |\n| Sustained need @ Stage 3 | 14.9 GB/s | **114.6 MB/s** |\n\n*Both \"sustained need\" figures are at Stage 3, so they compare like with like. The\n4.5 GB/s in the table above is the same design at Stage 1.*\n\n**K_max at Stage 3 is 1152.** We adopt **768** deliberately below the ceiling —\nD26 requires the sender to assume the weaker receiver, and the 200 MB/s budget is\nitself an unmeasured estimate (§18 R1). Margin at Stage 3: **1.74×**.\n\n| K | Block | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 128.0 KB | 19.7 MB/s | 39.3 MB/s | 69.5 MB/s | 2.88× margin |\n| **768** | **192.0 KB** | **32.4 MB/s** | **64.9 MB/s** | **114.6 MB/s** | **adopted, 1.74× margin** |\n| 1024 | 256.0 KB | 47.2 MB/s | 94.4 MB/s | 166.7 MB/s | 1.20× margin |\n| 1152 | 288.0 KB | 55.3 MB/s | 110.6 MB/s | 195.4 MB/s | 1.02× — the ceiling |\n| 1536 | 384.0 KB | 82.6 MB/s | 165.2 MB/s | 291.8 MB/s | 1.5× **over** at Stage 3 |\n\n### 3.1.1 L is set by the *conservative* ladder rung, not the nominal one\n\nA revision of this plan briefly set L = 507 B (\"one packet per v15 tile\") and broke\nD16's ladder. D15's source note states the governing rule plainly: **pick L to fit the\nsmallest tile any profile would use.** At L = 507 the packet is 520 B and the\nconservative rung, v10-L, holds **271 B** — so it could carry **zero** packets, only\nbeacons. That destroys the ladder's one load-bearing property: *a mis-guessed profile\nyields zero; a ladder always yields something.*\n\n**Rungs are therefore defined by packet count, with the QR version chosen to fit** —\nnot the reverse. At L = 256 B, packet = 13 + 256 = **269 B**:\n\n| Rung | Packets | Needs | QR version | Capacity | Waste |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| R1 conservative | 1 | 269 B | v10-L | 271 B | 2 B |\n| R2 nominal | 2 | 538 B | v16-L | 586 B | 48 B |\n| R3 aggressive | 3 | 807 B | v20-L | 858 B | 51 B |\n| R4 (probe only) | 4 | 1076 B | v23-L | 1091 B | 15 B |\n\nWaste stays ≤ 51 B on every rung. The pressure that motivated raising L has also\ngone: at K = 768 the mask term is K/8 = 96 B against a 256 B payload (27%), not the\n8× dominance that made L = 256 pathological at K = 16,384.\n\n**A rung MUST carry a whole number of packets.** Partial packets across tiles would\ncouple tiles together and destroy the independence D1 depends on.\n\n### 3.2 Neither side can hold the file in memory\n\nA multi-GB `Uint8Array` is not allocatable (Chrome's `ArrayBuffer` ceiling is ~2 GB;\nSafari's is lower), and would get a phone tab killed regardless.\n\n**Fix — D20:** stream both ends. `File.slice()` on the sender, OPFS on the receiver, one\nblock resident at a time.\n\n### 3.3 The whole-file hash cannot be computed in one pass\n\n`crypto.subtle.digest` has **no streaming API** — it takes one buffer.\n\n**Fix:** per-block hashes (cheap, and they let each block be written as it completes,\nthen verified retroactively once the manifest arrives) plus an optional whole-file hash\nfrom an incremental WASM hasher. See §7.4 for how this interacts with `streamId`.\n\n### 3.4 Miss recovery gets expensive as blocks multiply\n\nAt 192 KB per block a 4 GB file is ~21,800 blocks. Sequential dwell means a block missed\non pass 1 waits for pass 2 — hours. **Fix:** the repair code (§8.2), which makes recovery\nsub-minute and is why smaller blocks are affordable.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Decisions\n\n| # | Decision | Rationale | Source |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **D19** | **Block layer: independent 192.0 KB blocks, K = 768, L = 256 B** | GE cost is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). K = 768 keeps pace at Stage 3's 106 KB/s (114.6 MB/s needed, **1.74x margin**) within a conservative 200 MB/s phone-JS budget; matrix is 72.0 KB and the block-layer working set 264.0 KB, flat regardless of file size. K_max is 1152; 768 is deliberate conservatism per D26. **L is set by the conservative ladder rung** (S3.1.1), not the nominal one. What RFC 6330 calls source blocks. | §3.1, `sim/ge_cost_model.py` |\n| **D27** | **The receiver duty-cycles under thermal pressure; multi-GB is framed as multi-session** | Measured: a Pixel 6 hit 70 °C and its throttling threshold in **20–30 minutes**, against a §1.1 objective of 27 h–4 days of *continuous* decoding. Duty-cycling is **nearly free on this channel** — a skipped frame is an erasure the fountain code already absorbs (D5) — so 50% duty roughly halves heat for roughly half the rate, and **finishes** where 100% duty may not. Drop decode *resolution* before dropping frames (superlinearly cheaper). No web API exposes SoC temperature, so sustained fps decline is the proxy (E17b). | `spike-results`, R11 |\n| **D25** | **Cap fountain degree at d ≤ 64** | Cuts encoder XOR **7.9×** at the adopted K = 768 (mean degree 106.3 → 13.5): 12.2 MB/s → 1.6 MB/s at 450 packets/s (R2 nominal: 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps). D6 forbids changing the distribution on faith, so it was **simulated**: at the adopted **K = 768** the cap costs **+1.6 points** (1.34% → 2.97% mean, p99 4.2%), and +1.9 pts at K = 1024. There is a cliff below it — cap 32 costs +4.9 pts with a bad p99, cap 16 costs **+55 pts**. 64 is the right side of the cliff with margin. | `sim/degree_cap_sim.py` |\n| **D26** | **K is chosen by the SENDER at session start and MUST be conservative** | Decode cost lands on the receiver, whose CPU the sender cannot know (no back-channel). So the sender MUST assume the weaker device. K = 768 is the default floor; a sender-side setting MAY raise it when the user knows the receiver is a desktop. The receiver derives K from the beacon and MUST refuse a stream whose K exceeds what it benchmarked locally. | §3.1 |\n| **D20** | **Stream both ends; never materialise the file** | Multi-GB `ArrayBuffer` is not allocatable. `File.slice()` sender-side, OPFS receiver-side. | §3.2 |\n| **D21** | **Per-packet header stays 13 bytes: file metadata lives in the beacon** | A 3-byte block index would have cost 23% more header. Moving `payloadLen`, filename, MIME, hash and block count into the periodic beacon pays for it exactly. Payload packets carry only what is needed to *place bytes*. | §7.1 |\n| **D22** | **Resume is mandatory and first-class** | At 2.7–27 h for 1–10 GB, no transfer survives on user patience. Receiver persists the completed-block bitmap; incomplete blocks restart rather than persisting partial GE state. | §1.1, §8.3 |\n| **D23** | **Estimate time before the user commits; refuse or warn at defined thresholds** | Thresholds are numeric (§13.1), not \"a threshold\". Estimate from *measured* rate once acquired. | §1.1 |\n| **D24** | **Frames generated on demand and discarded; nothing pre-rendered** | The LT stream is endless — no finite frame set exists. One pass over 4 GB is ~550,000 frames = **4.2 TB** as `ImageData`. On-demand encode costs ~7% of one core. PRNG-derived indices make the sender **stateless**: frame *N* generates without replaying 1…*N*−1, which is what makes resume and repair nearly free. | §6.3.1 |\n| D1 | **Tiled QR, not single QR** | 15 × v15 QR decode from one 1080p frame in 7.8 ms for ~7.5 KB user-visible payload (at 2 packets/tile: 15 tiles × 2 packets × 256 B = 7,680 B; 8.0 KB includes 13-byte headers). This vs 2,953 B for one v40 — ~2.5× for zero new decoder risk. | `beyond-qr` §10 |\n| D2 | **QR v15 @ ECC L, ~15 tiles** | Bounded by the 4 **camera** px/module cliff (§2 — *not* screen px), not symbology density. EC L because the channel is erasure-dominated — redundancy belongs in the fountain code. L→H would cost 57% of payload for nothing. | `qr-encoding` |\n| D3 | **zxing-wasm decoder, read `.bytes`** | Only credible multi-symbol decoder that returns real bytes — verified against 7 libraries with every byte value: exact in 100% of payloads. Bounded 9–26 ms where jsQR hit 1453 ms. Apache-2.0. | `browser-qr-scanning` |\n| D4 | **node-qrcode encoder, mask pinned** | Pinning the mask is a 4.6–8× encode speedup — a bigger lever than library choice. Worker-safe. | `qr-encoding` |\n| D5 | **LT fountain + harmonic distribution + GF(2) Gaussian elimination** | GE needs +1.2% overhead at K=1000 where peeling needs +180%. ~300 lines. **Re-measured at the adopted K = 768**: +1.34% mean / +2.5% p99 uncapped, +2.97% / +4.2% with D25's cap — inside §13.1's budget. See §18 R1 for the RaptorQ trigger. | `fountain-codes`, `sim/` |\n| D6 | **Harmonic and GE are a coupled pair — never change one alone** | Harmonic + peeling is the worst cell measured and degrades as K grows. Fails only on large inputs, pointing away from the cause. Any change to the distribution (including D25's cap) MUST be simulated first. | `sim/` |\n| D7 | **Index sets derived from a PRNG, never transmitted** | Seeded on `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. Zero index bytes on the wire. | `fountain-codes` |\n| D8 | **Compress before blocking, to a staging file** | `CompressionStream` is native and streaming. Compress to OPFS first, then cut into fixed blocks — keeps K constant and derivable. Skip on already-compressed input (sample-detect). Staging MUST be wiped (§12, T4a). **Trade-off: with compression enabled, resume is NOT supported** (§8.3, `notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md`) — `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after staging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state. | `fountain-codes` |\n| D9 | **Display at ≤ half the *measured* camera fps** | PixNet's rule. Faster produces only torn frames. | `beyond-qr` |\n| D10 | **Every frame DC-balanced** | Stops auto-exposure hunting; throughput swings 2.4× on exposure. Also part of the photosensitivity mitigation (§20.1). | `custom-codec` |\n| D11 | **A runtime calibration probe decides luma-vs-colour, not this document** | Two research threads reached opposite conclusions (§6.6). The probe measures the device. | `beyond-qr` §6.6 |\n| D12 | **Dark-on-light, not dual-polarity** | Dual-polarity costs ~50% throughput. OLED ABL means mostly-white loses ~4× brightness — \"light\" means *moderate*. | `pwa-platform` |\n| D13 | **Add to Home Screen is mandatory on iOS** | Safari deletes service-worker caches after 7 days; Home Screen apps are exempt. | `pwa-platform` |\n| D14 | **`exposureCompensation: min`; measure delivered fps, never trust `getSettings()`** | A precondition for D9. Android delivers 15 fps while reporting 30/60; the fix measured 15.0 → 41.6 fps. Absent on iOS — hence \"measured\". | `browser-qr-scanning` §1.4 |\n| D15 | **Fragment length `L` is fixed for the session — not per profile, not ever** | Change L and K changes, invalidating every packet already collected. | `link-adaptation-design` |\n| D16 | **Sender mixes 2–4 robustness profiles *within every frame*; no negotiation in v1** | Packets are fungible, so the sender never has to choose. **Probing is free** — a probe tile that succeeds delivers real payload. Mixed within a frame so profiles cannot alias against camera fps. | `link-adaptation` |\n| D17 | **Conservative beacon profile, re-emitted periodically** | WiFi's lowest basic rate.
