Threat model\n967\t\n968\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n969\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n970\t\n971\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n972\t|---|---|---|---|\n973\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `fileSize` (281 TB), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `fileSize` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n974\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n975\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `fileSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n976\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n977\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The output **is** the deliverable — it cannot be deleted immediately. For sensitive files (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) indefinite storage is exposure. | **Mitigated.** Implement a deletion lifecycle: (1) delete after successful `share()`/`save()`; (2) reap orphaned outputs on startup; (3) warn before keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15); (4) provide a user-visible delete control. Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest. | integration: assert receiver OPFS empty after successful save; reap deletes orphans; UI has delete control; warning shown for partial artefacts |\n978\t| **T5** | **Supply chain.** The security claim depends on the bundle being what was audited. | **Partially mitigated.** `bf-13h` covers the output half (version footer + published hash). The input half — pinned dependency versions, WASM integrity, no post-install scripts — is a Phase 0 requirement (§14.5). | G3: lockfile diff + SRI check in CI |\n979\t| **T6** | **Shoulder-surfing / filming.** The optical channel is uniquely exposed: anyone with a camera in the room captures the same stream. | **Accepted for v1, consciously.** concept.md scopes encryption as a non-goal; §19 Q10 keeps it live. The app MUST NOT claim confidentiality it does not provide — the UI should say the transmission is visible to anyone who can see the screen. | none — accepted, not mitigated |\n980\t| **T7** | **No telemetry, by construction.** | **Committed.** The app makes **zero** network requests after load. Enforced by CI (§14.4) and by A8. This is a stronger and more checkable claim than a privacy policy. | §14.4 network assertion + A8 |\n981\t\n982\t**Out of scope for v1, stated:** authenticating the *sender* (no PKI, no trust anchor); a\n983\tmalicious *receiver* (it only gets what it is shown); side-channels other than the optical\n984\tone; physical device compromise.\n985\t\n986\t---\n987\t\n988\t## 13. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n989\t\n990\t### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n991\t\n992\t§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n993\t\n994\t**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n995\t- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n996\t- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n997\t- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n998\t\n999\tThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n1000\t**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). After fountain (+12%) and 30% erasure,\n1001\tnet goodput is **~70 KB/s** — well above the 20 KB/s budget.\n1002\t\n1003\t| Budget | Value | Gate |\n1004\t|---|---|---|\n1005\t| Throughput, A1 reference setup | **≥ 20 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3 |\n1006\t| Throughput, A3 phone→phone | **≥ 3 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3; miss triggers §18 R4 |\n1007\t| Block-layer working set | **≤ 1 MB**, any file size (I6a) | Phase 1 |\n1008\t| Whole-receiver peak | **≤ 64 MB**, ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s (I6b) | Phase 3 |\n1009\t| GE sustained XOR need | **≤ 200 MB/s** at the fastest supported stage (modelled 114.6 MB/s, 1.74× margin) — **measured 3,260 MB/s desktop / ~815 MB/s est. phone; the budget was ~16× pessimistic.** R1 provisionally closed, pending an on-device run *while thermally throttled* | Phase 1 + G7 |\n1010\t| Per-camera-frame decode | **≤ 60 ms** p99 (leaves headroom at 15 fps) — **measured 67–69 ms p50 full-frame, 194 ms at 4K, 6.6 ms with a tight ROI. p50 already exceeds the p99 budget**; the fixes (worker pool §6.2, tight ROI §6.4) are unimplemented, so this is violated by the instrument, not yet by the design | Phase 3 |\n1011\t| Encode + render per frame | **≤ 20 ms** p99 — **measured ~150 ms** (6.7 fps against 12 requested) on a 2015 laptop with D4's pinned mask unimplemented | Phase 3 |\n1012\t| Time-to-first-packet after aim | **≤ 3 s** p50 | Phase 5 |\n1013\t| Reception overhead vs K | **≤ +5%** mean, **≤ +12%** p99 (measured: +2.97% / +4.2%) | Phase 1, `sim/` |\n1014\t| **Sustained operation duration** | **≥ 20 min** sustained throughput within **30% of initial rate** on target phone (Pixel 6-class) without active cooling. This is the **minimum viable duration** before R11's thermal throttling mitigation (duty-cycle reduction) must engage. The system is not required to avoid throttling indefinitely—only to (a) sustain long enough for practical use and (b) detect and surface throttling when it occurs (E17b, D27). | Phase 3; validated by T-long-run |\n1015\t| **Warn threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 30 min** → explicit confirm | Phase 4 |\n1016\t| **Refuse threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 24 h**, or quota insufficient → refuse with an override | Phase 4 |\n1017\t\n1018\t### 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n1019\t\n1020\tEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n1021\t\n1022\t| Parameter | Reference value |\n1023\t|---|---|\n1024\t| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes. With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n1025\t| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n1026\t| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n1027\t| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n1028\t| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n1029\t| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n1030\t| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n1031\t| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n1032\t| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n1033\t\n1034\t**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\n1035\ta 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\n1036\tto handheld numbers.\n1037\t\n1038\t---\n1039\t\n1040\t## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n1041\t\n1042\t### 14.1 Tiers\n1043\t\n1044\t| Tier | What | Runs |\n1045\t|---|---|---|\n1046\t| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n1047\t| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n1048\t| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n1049\t| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n1050\t| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n1051\t| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,800 blocks | Nightly |\n1052\t| **T-long-run** | **20–30 minute sustained run** on real devices to validate thermal behavior (R11), duty-cycle economics (D27), and sustained throughput. Tracks fps decline, decode rate, and effective goodput over time. **This is the ONLY tier that can measure R11 and D27** — the 60 s floor in §13.2 structurally excludes thermal phenomena. | Weekly (or per thermal-related change) |\n1053\t| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n1054\t| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n1055\t\n1056\t> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n1057\t> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n1058\t\n1059\t### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n1060\t\n1061\t**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\n1062\trejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\n1063\tround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\n1064\tincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n1065\t**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\n1066\tthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n1067\t\n1068\t### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n1069\t\n1070\tShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n1071\t\n1072\t- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n1073\t- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n1074\t- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n1075\t- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n1076\t- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n1077\t  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n1078\t\n1079\t### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n1080\t\n1081\tCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\n1082\tincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\n1083\tdoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n1084\t(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\n1085\texecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n1086\t\n1087\t### 14.5 Quality gates\n1088\t\n1089\t| Gate | Requirement |\n1090\t|---|---|\n1091\t| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n1092\t| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n1093\t| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n1094\t| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n1095\t| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n1096\t| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n1097\t| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. A green build\n1101\tassembled from different commits is not a green build.\n1102\t\n1103\t### 14.6 Definition of done\n1104\t\n1105\tA phase is done when: its exit criteria (§17) are met; G1–G5 are green on one commit; every\n1106\tnew failure mode has a test; every new error code has a user-facing string; and the plan\n1107\tis updated if any decision changed.\n1108\t\n1109\t**Stop-ship criteria** — do not release if: any A-scenario fails; I1–I10 are unenforced;\n1110\ta data-loss path exists without a test; or the version footer is absent (a user cannot\n1111\ttell what they are running).\n1112\t\n1113\t---\n1114\t\n1115\t## 15. Platform and operations\n1161\t\n1162\t### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n1163\t\n1164\t- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n1165\t- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n1166\t  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n1167\t  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n1168\t- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n1169\t  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n1170\t- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n1171\t- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n1172\t- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n1173\t  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n1174\t- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n1175\t  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n1176\t- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n1177\t- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n1178\t\n1179\t### 16.2 Deployment\n1180\t\n1181\tStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\n1182\tNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n1183\t**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n1184\t\n1185\t### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n1186\t\n1187\tTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\n1188\ta service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\n1189\tbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n1190\t\n1191\t| Rule | |\n1192\t|---|---|\n1193\t| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n1194\t| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n1195\t| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n1196\t| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n1197\t| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n1198\t| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n1199\t| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n1200\t\n1201\t### 16.4 Health check\n1202\t\n1203\tOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\n1204\tthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\n1205\tlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It refuses or warns\n1206\t**as one gate** with numeric thresholds (§13.1) rather than as three separate surprises.\n1207\t\n1208\t---\n1209\t\n1210\t## 17. It\n1261\tdecides **what numbers to build it with**, and those numbers are encoded in the\n1262\tframing layer that Phase 1 writes:\n1263\t\n1264\t| Parameter | Basis today | Sets |\n1265\t|---|---|---|\n1266\t| Tiling gain (~10×) | measured on *simulated* camera paths | D1, the throughput thesis |\n1267\t| Erasure 20–30% | **assumption** (D18c states this) | dwell = 1.6 K (§8.1) |\n1268\t| 4 px/module cliff | other devices | D2, §3.1.1's rungs, `bf-1g0` |\n1269\t| Delivered fps | a Pixel 6, not ours | D9, D14 |\n1270\t| 200 MB/s JS XOR | ~~unmeasured guess~~ **measured: 3,260 MB/s desktop (S1)** | D19's K = 768 |\n1271\t\n1272\tIt is cheap *precisely because* it skips everything this plan carefully designs: no\n1273\tfountain code, no blocks, no compression, no resume, no OPFS, no UI. T-physical-rig substitutes | If field failures are suspected → voluntary copyable benchmark string (ledger, currently cut) |\n1312\t| **R9** | **Multi-hour transfers die to backgrounding / sleep / thermal** | **High** | Medium | E8, E17, wake lock, resume (D22) | Resume proves insufficient → reduce block size further so less is lost |\n1313\t| **R10** | **A wire-version bump strands cached receivers** | Medium | Medium | §16.3 one-way-door rule | Skew observed → extend the soak period before bumping |\n1314\t| **R12** | **Residual erasure exceeds the assumed 20–30% band** | **High** — measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | **High** — D18c, the §8.1 dwell budget and every §13.1 throughput figure rest on this band | Raise dwell; promote the repair code (§8.2). Note v1 cannot *observe* erasure (D18a), so this is an assumption, not a controlled quantity | Erasure > 35% under §13.2 conditions → the **repair code becomes the primary recovery path, not the tail**, and dwell is re-derived from the measured band |\n1315\t| **R11** | **Thermal throttling makes long transfers self-defeating** | **High** (observed first session) | **High** — attacks the multi-GB objective directly | Duty-cycling (D27), decode-resolution drop, resume (D22). Self-reinforcing loop: SoC slows → decode slower → camera fps falls → erasure rises → transfer lengthens → more heat | Sustained fps decline > 30% from a cool start → drop duty cycle and **tell the user**, rather than silently running hot and slow. If duty-cycling cannot hold the rate, reframe multi-GB as a multi-session workflow (§1.1) |\n1316\t\n1317\t---\n1318\t\n1319\t## 18.1 Anti-patterns — mistakes this project has already made\n1320\t\n1321\tEvery entry below was made *in this repo* and cost real time. They are collected here because\n1322\teach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\n1323\tstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n1324\t\n1325\t| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n1326\t|---|---|---|---|\n1327\t| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n1328\t| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n1329\t| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n1330\t| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n1331\t| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n1332\t| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n1333\t| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n1334\t| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n1335\t| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n1336\t| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n1337\t\n1338\t## 18.2 Proof obligations\n1339\t\n1340\tEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. This exists\n1341\tbecause the project has a documented history of confident-and-wrong (AP1, AP3, AP4, plus a\n1342\t2× formula error), and G7 only makes *one* class of claim executable.\n1343\t\n1344\t| Assumption | Holds iff | Invalidating evidence | Fallback |\n1345\t|---|---|---|---|\n1346\t| D19's K = 768 | phone GE ≥ 114.6 MB/s sustained **while thermally throttled** | on-device benchmark under load | K → 512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 vs wirehair (R1) |\n1347\t| S1's ÷4 phone factor | desktop-to-phone JS gap ≤ 4× | on-device `ge-bench.mjs` | recompute K from the measured figure |\n1348\t| D18c's 20–30% erasure | erasure under §13.2 conditions stays ≤ 30% | measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | repair code (§8.2) becomes the primary path, not the tail (R12) |\n1349\t| The 4 camera px/module cliff | zxing needs ≥ 4 camera px/module under handheld blur | S3 distance sweep under §13.2 conditions | re-derive the rung ladder from the measured cliff |\n1350\t| D1's ~10× tiling gain | holds on hardware, not just simulated camera paths | rung sweep on the rig | drop to fewer, larger tiles |\n1351\t| D27's duty-cycle economics | 50% duty ≈ 50% heat and completes | long-run thermal profile | multi-session framing (§1.1), or cap the supported file size |\n1352\t| Stage 3's value | decode CPU/bit beats QR's | prototype against a worker-pool QR baseline | stay at Stage 2 |\n1353\t\n1354\t## 19. Open questions\n1355\t\n1356\t1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n1357\t   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. Porting is legal but makes the repo\n1358\t   mixed-license and obliges per-file marking. The failure mode is someone pasting in a\n1359\t   function and deciding this by accident. → [`prior-art-libcimbar.md`](../notes/prior-art-libcimbar.md)\n1360\t2. **Optimal K and block size on real hardware.** §3.1 is a model, not a measurement.\n1361\t   Resolve in Phase 1 (R1).\n1362\t3. **Phone→phone viability** at 54 cells. Resolve in Phase 3 (R4).\n1363\t4. **Progress UX with no back-channel.** The sender cannot know receiver progress. Over a\n1364\t   10-hour transfer this matters far more than over 30 seconds. **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n1365\t5. **Should the sender ever stop?** It loops forever; at GB scale \"forever\" may be days.\n1366\t   **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n1367\t6. **Delta transfer vs fixed blocks** — see §20.2. **Resolve before Phase 4 implementation.**\n1368\t7. **Closed-loop negotiation — deferred on evidence.** Bidirectional links are precedented\n1369\t   (MAMBA: two phones, 11–28 kbps each way), but MAMBA's measured gain from closing the\n1370\t   loop is only **5–20%**, while changing the coding paradigm buys multiples. Reassess\n1371\t   after Phase 4. → [`link-adaptation-design.md`](../notes/link-adaptation-design.md)\n1372\t8. **SoftLight-style soft hints — the highest-ceiling idea we are not doing.** Per-bit\n1373\t   confidence plus a false-positive-tolerant rateless code: **2.2× with fixed parameters**.\n1374\t   Blocked on zxing returning hard bytes; natural fit for Stage 3.\n1375\t9. **Multi-GB export on iOS** (R5). Detect up front, never at hour 9.\n1376\t10. **Encryption.** Out of scope for v1 (T6), but the optical channel is uniquely exposed\n1377\t    to filming. Platform and operations\n\n### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n\n- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n\n### 16.2 Deployment\n\nStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\nNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n\n### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n\nTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\na service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\nbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n\n| Rule | |\n|---|---|\n| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n\n### 16.4 Health check\n\nOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\nthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\nlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It refuses or warns\n**as one gate** with numeric thresholds (§13.1) rather than as three separate surprises.\n\n---\n\n## 17. The spike does not decide **whether** to build the codec — the\nfountain code, block layer and framing are needed whatever the channel does. It\ndecides **what numbers to build it with**, and those numbers are encoded in the\nframing layer that Phase 1 writes:\n\n| Parameter | Basis today | Sets |\n|---|---|---|\n| Tiling gain (~10×) | measured on *simulated* camera paths | D1, the throughput thesis |\n| Erasure 20–30% | **assumption** (D18c states this) | dwell = 1.6 K (§8.1) |\n| 4 px/module cliff | other devices | D2, §3.1.1's rungs, `bf-1g0` |\n| Delivered fps | a Pixel 6, not ours | D9, D14 |\n| 200 MB/s JS XOR | ~~unmeasured guess~~ **measured: 3,260 MB/s desktop (S1)** | D19's K = 768 |\n\nIt is cheap *precisely because* it skips everything this plan carefully designs: no\nfountain code, no blocks, no compression, no resume, no OPFS, no UI. A full\nGE decode of one block at K = 768 takes **8 ms** at **3,260 MB/s** on the dev\nmachine — the 200 MB/s budget was ~16× pessimistic, leaving **7.1× margin at\nStage 3** even after a harsh ÷4 phone factor. **R1 is provisionally closed**, pending\na re-run in a browser on the target phone; the ÷4 factor is itself a guess.\n\nS2–S4 (rung sweep, distance sweep, handheld and phone→phone) need the optical rig and\ntwo devices. Block layer,\nframing, session ≈ 800. Modulation Stage 1 ≈ 600. Receiver pipeline ≈ 700. App shell, UI,\ncoaching ≈ 1500 — **Phase 5 is the largest single phase**, which the phase ordering hides.\n\n---\n\n## 18. They are collected here because\neach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\nstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n\n| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n\n## 18.2 Proof obligations\n\nEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. This exists\nbecause the project has a documented history of confident-and-wrong (AP1, AP3, AP4, plus a\n2× formula error), and G7 only makes *one* class of claim executable.\n\n| Assumption | Holds iff | Invalidating evidence | Fallback |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| D19's K = 768 | phone GE ≥ 114.6 MB/s sustained **while thermally throttled** | on-device benchmark under load | K → 512 (2.88× margin), then re-open D5 vs wirehair (R1) |\n| S1's ÷4 phone factor | desktop-to-phone JS gap ≤ 4× | on-device `ge-bench.mjs` | recompute K from the measured figure |\n| D18c's 20–30% erasure | erasure under §13.2 conditions stays ≤ 30% | measured 48% (non-qualifying conditions) | repair code (§8.2) becomes the primary path, not the tail (R12) |\n| The 4 camera px/module cliff | zxing needs ≥ 4 camera px/module under handheld blur | S3 distance sweep under §13.2 conditions | re-derive the rung ladder from the measured cliff |\n| D1's ~10× tiling gain | holds on hardware, not just simulated camera paths | rung sweep on the rig | drop to fewer, larger tiles |\n| D27's duty-cycle economics | 50% duty ≈ 50% heat and completes | long-run thermal profile | multi-session framing (§1.1), or cap the supported file size |\n| Stage 3's value | decode CPU/bit beats QR's | prototype against a worker-pool QR baseline | stay at Stage 2 |\n\n## 19. Open questions\n\n1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. Adopted roadmap items\n\nFrom [`ideas-ledger.md`](../notes/ideas-ledger.md) (103 generated → 10 finalists → 7\nadopted). Tracked as beads blocking genesis `bf-28p`.\n\n| Bead | Item | Grade | Phase |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `bf-4d6` | Storage pre-flight and capacity gate | S | 4 |\n| `bf-5vm` | Diagnostic stall detector | M | 5 |\n| `bf-1g0` | Aim reticle and distance coach | M | 5 |\n| `bf-6d3` | Photosensitivity safeguard (WCAG 2.3.1) | S | 5 |\n| `bf-280` | Delta transfer and cross-session resume | L | 4+ |\n| `bf-4tb` | Pairing splash QR | S | 5 |\n| `bf-13h` | Verifiable build + version footer | M | 0 |\n\n**Rejected:** *text/secret fast path* (a different product inside this one) and\n*single-file HTML build* (deploying as a static site, and WASM is required — exactly what\nsingle-file cannot cleanly inline). The PWA offline story is unaffected.\n\n### 20.1 Photosensitivity changes a rendering decision (`bf-6d3`)\n\nWCAG 2.3.1 caps general flashes at three per second **or** requires the flashing area to\nstay under the small-safe threshold. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\nhours is a genuine seizure risk.\n\n**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\nfewer cells → less throughput. The compliant design is therefore **a bounded coded region\ninside a static surround**, not full-bleed, and the area cost MUST be measured in Phase 3\nrather than assumed. D10's DC balancing is part of this mitigation, not just an\nauto-exposure fix: constant mean luminance is far less provocative than alternating fields.\n\n### 20.2 Delta transfer tensions with the block design (`bf-280`)\n\n**A partially-received file *is* \"a file the receiver already has\"** — so\nresume-after-interruption and delta transfer are one mechanism at two granularities.\n\nBut general delta wants **content-defined chunking** (rolling hash, variable boundaries),\nwhich contradicts I1 (L fixed) and D19 (fixed blocks, K derived). Two ways out:\n\n1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n   stays untouched.\n2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n   everything after it.\n\nOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\nwhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\nnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n\n---\n\n## 21. verification failure prevents completion and triggers E-BLOCK-HASH\"\n\n## Why This Resolution\n\n### Rejected Alternative: Require manifest before any OPFS write\n\nThe task description noted:\n> \"Retroactive verification means re-reading and re-hashing every written block — a full extra pass, currently unbudgeted\"\n\nWaiting for the manifest before any OPFS write would create a critical problem:\n\n1. **Manifest acquisition window**: For a 4 GB file, the beacon cadence (~2 s) means ~12 minutes to acquire the full manifest\n2. **Blocked progress**: During this window, no blocks could be written to OPFS, forcing them to be held in memory\n3. **Memory pressure**: At 21,845 blocks for 4 GB, holding all decoded blocks in memory would violate I6a (≤ 1 MB block-layer working set)\n4. **Resume fragility**: If the receiver reloaded during the manifest window (bf-17s0 notes show this is a real scenario), all progress would be lost\n\n### Chosen Alternative: Write but never surface\n\nThe \"written but unverified, never surfaced\" approach:\n\n1. **Allows progress**: Blocks are written to OPFS as they complete, avoiding memory pressure\n2. **Maintains safety**: Unverified blocks are never exported or surfaced to the user\n3. **Enables resume**: The `writtenBlocks` bitmap preserves progress across reloads (§8.3)\n4. **Efficient verification**: Once the manifest arrives, verification is a simple hash comparison per block\n\n## Implementation Details\n\n### Two-Bitmap System (§7.6)\n\n- **`complete` bitmap**: Tracks blocks that have reached rank K (decoded)\n- **`writtenBlocks` bitmap**: Tracks blocks that have been written to OPFS\n- **Verified blocks**: Only when manifest arrives and hash passes\n\n### E12 Edge Case Handling\n\nFrom §11, E12:\n> \"Block hash verification fails. After manifest arrives, block hash verification fails. Clear the verified bitmap bit, re-collect the block. Emit `E-BLOCK-HASH`. Block may already be written to OPFS but is never surfaced until verified (I9).\"\n\nThis handles the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) where a corrupted payload passes `fcrc` check.\n\n### Resume Behavior (§8.3)\n\n> \"Pre-manifest reload behavior: If the receiver is reloaded before the manifest arrives, the persisted bitmap preserves which blocks were decoded, and the written blocks remain in OPFS. The `writtenBlocks` bitmap is reset on resume, and blocks are re-verified once the manifest arrives. This prevents losing all received blocks during the manifest acquisition window.\"\n\n## Consistency Verification\n\nThe resolution is consistent across the plan:\n\n1. **I9** (invariants table): \"MAY be written... but MUST NOT be surfaced\"\n2. **§7.6**: \"written to OPFS but tracked separately from verified blocks\"\n3. **§6.4** (receiver pipeline): \"rank == K → write to OPFS → mark decode bitmap → verify hash (if manifest present) → mark verified bitmap\"\n4. **E12**: \"Block may already be written to OPFS but is never surfaced until verified (I9)\"\n\n## References\n\n- plan.md §5 (Invariants): I9 definition and enforcement\n- plan.md §7.6: Block-hash manifest and two-bitmap system\n- plan.md §11 (Error taxonomy): E12 handling\n- plan.md §8.3: Resume behavior\n- Commit d1e4b9b: \"gap-review round 2: fix the integrity story and the CDN default\"\n- Commit 8abd3ea: \"docs(bf-5od): re-spec manifest as fixed-K multi-block stream\"\n- Commit 74a5e3c: \"docs(bf-28b): resolve I5 contradiction for concurrent manifest GE context\"\n","numLines":90,"startLine":1,"totalLines":90}}}
